lines.junior: Use the note, the yard book, an older note and the story of the palace.
lines.master: Draw on the note, the yard book, an older note and the palace's story.

lines.rookie: The Daewongun has heard the truth!
lines.junior: The Daewongun has learned the truth!
lines.master: The truth has reached the Daewongun!

lines.rookie: Mr. Pyo's cart turns back to the timber yard.
lines.junior: Mr. Pyo's cart heads back to the timber yard.
lines.master: Mr. Pyo's cart rumbles back to the timber yard.

lines.rookie: The ten logs will stand in the palace gates.
lines.junior: The ten logs will become part of the palace gates.
lines.master: The ten logs will take their place in the palace gates.

lines.rookie: Duri lays three notes side by side.
lines.junior: Duri places three notes next to each other.
lines.master: Duri lays out three notes, side by side.

lines.rookie: Answer each question with its own evidence.
lines.junior: Answer every question with the right evidence.
lines.master: Meet each question with its own evidence.

lines.rookie: Show the Daewongun what happened to the logs, and what the palace costs.
lines.junior: Show the Daewongun what happened to the logs and what the palace costs.
lines.master: Reveal to the Daewongun what became of the logs, and what the palace costs.

lines.rookie: These logs are marked 다. They are not for my palace.
lines.junior: These logs have the mark 다. They aren't meant for my palace.
lines.master: These logs bear the mark 다. They are not destined for my palace.

lines.rookie: Look closely, sir.
lines.junior: Take a closer look, sir.
lines.master: Look more closely, sir.

lines.rookie: Why rebuild the palace?
lines.junior: Why are you rebuilding the palace?
lines.master: Why rebuild the palace at all?

lines.rookie: The great palace burned in a war long ago.
lines.junior: The great palace burned down in a war long ago.
lines.master: The great palace burned in a war, long ago.

lines.rookie: I want it to stand again.
lines.junior: I want to see it standing again.
lines.master: I mean to see it stand once more.

lines.rookie: The Daewongun asks: "How do you know they are palace logs?"
lines.junior: The Daewongun asks: "How do you know these are palace logs?"
lines.master: The Daewongun asks: "How do you know they belong to the palace?"

lines.rookie: One cut on each mark is new. 나 became 다.
lines.junior: Each mark has one new cut. 나 turned into 다.
lines.master: On each mark, one cut is fresh. 나 became 다.

lines.rookie: One more line. Clever, and wrong.
lines.junior: Just one more line. Clever, but wrong.
lines.master: A single extra line. Clever, and wrong.

lines.rookie: That does not show the new cut.
lines.junior: That doesn't show the new cut.
lines.master: That reveals nothing of the new cut.

lines.rookie: The water-drop note says one mark has a new line.
lines.junior: The water-drop note says that one mark has a new line.
lines.master: According to the water-drop note, one mark has a new line.

lines.rookie: The Daewongun asks: "How many of my logs?"
lines.junior: The Daewongun asks: "How many of my logs were taken?"
lines.master: The Daewongun asks: "How many of my logs?"

lines.rookie: Ten. The yard book shows ten 나 logs became 다.
lines.junior: Ten. The yard book shows that ten 나 logs became 다.
lines.master: Ten. The yard book records ten 나 logs turning into 다.

lines.rookie: Ten great logs! Take them back to the yard.
lines.junior: Ten great logs! Bring them back to the yard.
lines.master: Ten great logs! Return them to the yard.

lines.rookie: That does not count the logs.
lines.junior: That doesn't count the logs.
lines.master: That offers no count of the logs.

lines.rookie: The yard book counts the logs.
lines.junior: The logs are counted in the yard book.
lines.master: The yard book holds the count of the logs.

lines.rookie: The Daewongun asks: "And who nailed this note in my yard?"
lines.junior: The Daewongun asks: "And who nailed this note up in my yard?"
lines.master: The Daewongun asks: "And who dared nail this note in my yard?"

lines.rookie: The same water drop was on notes in 1592 and 1795.
lines.junior: Notes in 1592 and 1795 had the same water drop.
lines.master: That same water drop marked notes in 1592 and 1795.

lines.rookie: Then no one person wrote them all.
lines.junior: Then they were not all written by one person.
lines.master: Then no single person could have written them all.

lines.rookie: That has no water drop.
lines.junior: That one has no water drop.
lines.master: No water drop there.

lines.rookie: The note of 1795 has the same water drop.
lines.junior: The 1795 note has the same water drop.
lines.master: The note of 1795 bears the same water drop.

lines.rookie: The Daewongun asks: "Wood is not all a palace needs, is it?"
lines.junior: The Daewongun asks: "A palace needs more than wood, doesn't it?"
lines.master: The Daewongun asks: "Wood alone does not make a palace, does it?"

lines.rookie: It needs money and work from the people too.
lines.junior: It needs the people's money and work as well.
lines.master: It demands money and labour from the people as well.

lines.rookie: And since the new coin came, prices have gone up.
lines.junior: And prices have risen since the new coin came.
lines.master: And ever since the new coin came, prices have climbed.

lines.rookie: The palace will be finished.
lines.junior: The palace will be finished.
lines.master: The palace will be completed.

lines.rookie: That does not show what the palace costs.
lines.junior: That doesn't show what the palace costs.
lines.master: That reveals nothing of what the palace costs.

lines.rookie: The palace's story names the money, the new coin and the prices.
lines.junior: The story of the palace mentions the money, the new coin and the prices.
lines.master: The palace's story names the money, the new coin and the rising prices.

lines.rookie: CLOSE THE CASE
lines.junior: CLOSE THE CASE
lines.master: CLOSE THE CASE

lines.rookie: The rebuilding had begun in the fourth month of 1865.
lines.junior: The rebuilding had started in the fourth month of 1865.
lines.master: Rebuilding had begun in the fourth month of 1865.

lines.rookie: In 1868 the palace was finished, and the King moved in.
lines.junior: The palace was finished in 1868, and the King moved in.
lines.master: In 1868 the palace stood complete, and the King took up residence.

lines.rookie: It cost the people dearly: forced gifts, high prices and hard work.
lines.junior: The people paid a high price: forced gifts, high prices and hard work.
lines.master: The people paid dearly: forced gifts, soaring prices and hard labour.

lines.rookie: I wrote the note. My father taught me the mark.
lines.junior: I'm the one who wrote the note. My father taught me the mark.
lines.master: The note was mine. My father taught me the mark.

lines.rookie: 1592, 1795, 1866: the same water drop.
lines.junior: 1592, 1795, 1866: always the same water drop.
lines.master: 1592, 1795, 1866: one and the same water drop.

lines.rookie: Not one person. A family keeps writing them. But why?
lines.junior: Not one person, but a family that keeps writing them. But why?
lines.master: Not one person, but a family, still writing them. Yet why?
